title: QBR: Strategy Sprint Deck Kits (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose: a compact, outcomes-first QBR deck kit designed for a 2-hour "strategy sprint" with customers. Two variants included: Standard (fast cadence, product-led companies) and Enterprise (multi-stakeholder, renewal-focused). This is a working kit — includes slide titles, short speaker notes, a renewal tracker template, escalation playbook, and appendix snippets.

QUICK NOTES / HOW TO USE
- Goal: align on outcomes, surface blockers, and create a concrete renewal/expansion plan with owners + dates during the meeting.
- Timing: Standard = 45–60 minute QBR; Enterprise = 90–120 minute strategy sprint with breakout tracks.
- Prep: send pre-read 3 business days ahead (1-page health snapshot + top 3 agenda asks).
- Audience guidance: invite exec sponsor, product owner, tech lead, and CS AM for all Enterprise sprints.

WHEN TO PICK WHICH KIT
- Standard: customers <= $50k ARR, PLG-first, cadence: quarterly or bi-quarterly. Use when adoption signals are healthy and renewal risk low.
- Enterprise: customers > $250k ARR, multi-product deployments, security/compliance slippage, or when renewal is within 6 months.

STANDARD DECK (clean, 8–10 slides; ~45–60m)
1) Title & Outcome (1 slide)
   - One-line meeting goal (e.g., "Align on FY26 priorities + renewal posture")
   - Suggested visual: single sentence outcome card + 3 bullets of desired decisions
2) Executive Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Top metrics: ARR, NRR if applicable, usage (calls/minute, tokens/month, embeddings ops), latency SLA breaches last 90d
   - Speaker note: "We want the exec to leave confident about product value and a single ask."
3) What’s Changed Since Last QBR (1 slide)
   - 3 quick wins and 2 friction points (product + ops)
   - Links to relevant tickets (e.g., JIRA) or incidents
4) Adoption & Value Flow (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Adoption funnel (launched features -> active users -> automation wins) with a small pipeline chart
   - Slide B: Customer stories / one short quote + impact (# saved hrs, % reduction in latency/cost)
5) Quality and Cost Signals (1 slide)
   - Cost per inference trend, quantization/compaction experiments, error/regression hotspots
6) Roadmap Alignment & Opportunities (1–2 slides)
   - Proposed product bets prioritized by customer impact and engineering effort
7) Renewal & Ask Ladder (1 slide)
   - Clear ask(s) with tiers (commit, feature access, exec sponsor time) + timeline
8) Action Plan & Owners (1 slide)
   - 90-day plan: owner, metric, due date

SPEAKER NOTES EXAMPLES (standard)
- Exec Snapshot: "Key signal is the 28% increase in inference requests — shows adoption but cost per 1k tokens rose; recommend experiment X.
- Ask Ladder: "If you can commit to this usage floor we can guarantee latency SLA + 10% discount for reserved capacity."

ENTERPRISE DECK (robust, 16–22 slides + appendix; ~90–120m)
Structure: Opening (alignment) -> Health deep-dive -> Technical appendix -> Joint roadmap + commercial plan -> Renewal negotiation ladder -> Breakouts -> Close
1) Title + Sprint Outcomes (1 slide)
2) Executive Health Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Add: Contract start/end, current billing cadence, previous renewal adjustments
3) Stakeholder Map & RACI (1 slide)
   - Include names, influence level, open asks required for renewal
4) Product Adoption Deep-dive (2 slides)
   - Feature-level adoption by team, query patterns, KV cache hit ratios, common prompt templates in use
5) Performance & Reliability (2 slides)
   - Latency p95/p99 trends, incident postmortems summary, fallback events to lower-tier models
6) Cost Efficiency & Optimization Opportunities (2 slides)
   - Cost by model/route, potential savings via batching/quantized variants, Redwood Optimize recommendations
7) Security & Compliance Check (1 slide)
   - KMS/HSM integrations, audit log gaps, private deployment blockers
8) Joint Roadmap Workshop (2 slides)
   - 3 priority bets, required commitments, decision gates
9) Commercial & Renewal Strategy (2 slides)
   - Ask ladder, concession boundaries, enterprise legal/po timelines
10) Breakout Instructions + Templates (1 slide)
   - 3 parallel tracks: Exec/Outcomes, Engineering/Technical, Procurement/Legal
11) Final Commitments & Next Steps (1 slide)

APPENDIX SAMPLES (copy/repurpose)
- Technical Appendix: sample API usage patterns, KV cache config, infra topology diagram (text description), expected token distribution.
- Data needed for procurement: SOW template excerpt, data residency attestation checklist, support SLAs.

RENEWAL TRACKER (plain-text table — paste into sheet)
Columns: Customer | Renewal Date | Current ARR | Renewal Type (renew/expand/churn) | Score (1-10) | Exec Sponsor | Tech Owner | Major Open Issues | Last Contact | Next Action | Owner | Due Date | Notes
Sample row: Acme AI | 2026-06-30 | $420,000 | renew+expand | 7 | Jane R. (Customer) | Tom L. (Eng) | KV cache performance | 2026-01-18 | Contract proposal sent | Aisha K. | 2026-02-02 | Need legal redline

RISK SCORING RUBRIC (use numeric then color code in deck)
- 8–10 (red): Active procurement/legal blockers; >15% negative trend in key adoption metric; exec sponsor missing for >2 qtrs
- 5–7 (amber): Mixed adoption; open technical debt >2 items impacting SLA; renewal in 3–6 months
- 1–4 (green): Healthy adoption, roadmap aligned, renewal >6 months

RENEWAL PLAYBOOK (step-by-step; short)
1) T-90 days: Health sync + renewal tracker updated; confirm exec sponsor. Owner: AM.
2) T-60 days: Commercial proposal drafted; procurement checklist started (legal + security). Owner: AM + Sales Eng.
3) T-45 days: Technical deep-dive w/ Eng Solutions; lineup any migration or private deployment POCs. Owner: Solutions Eng.
4) T-30 days: Exec alignment meeting; present ask ladder; lock commercial terms. Owner: AM + Sales Leader.
5) T-7 days: Legal signoff queue + finance invoicing setup. Owner: Legal + Finance.

ESCALATION & CONCESSION GUIDE (enterprise)
- If risk score >=8: create "Urgent Renewal War Room" channel, daily standup until resolution.
- Typical concessions and thresholds: 5% discount for 12-month commit; 10–15% discount requires CSM+Sales+RevOps approval and >$500k ARR.
- Always exchange something of value for a concession: faster migration plan, extended trial of Dedicated pool, or embedding of Redwood Optimize credits.

VISUALS / CHART TEMPLATES (slide copy prompts)
- Adoption funnel: "Launched -> Piloting -> Active -> Automating" (bars + delta % vs last Q)
- Cost curve: time-series line with callouts when quantization or batching was enabled
- Ask ladder: stacked cards (Commit tier A / B / C) + decision timeline

MEETING FACILITATION CHECKLIST (for CS lead)
- Pre-read sent? (Y/N)
- Stakeholders invited and confirmed? (list names)
- Data validated (billing, usage, incidents)? (Y/N)
- Breakout facilitators assigned? (Y/N)
- Post-meeting notes + owner list ready to share within 24 hours

TEMPLATED EMAILS (short)
- Pre-read invite: "Hello <Name>, attached is a 1-page health snapshot and the proposed outcomes for our upcoming QBR (date). Please confirm any additional topics. — Aisha"
- Post-QBR recap: "Thanks all — attached: committed actions, owners, dates, and the proposed contract term. Please comment on redlined items by EOD x."

APPENDIX: SAMPLE ACTION LOG (copy into your CRM)
- ActionID | Action | Owner | Priority | Due Date | Status | Notes
- A-001 | Provision Dedicated burst pool for perf test | Tom L. | High | 2026-03-10 | Open | Need infra approval

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOS (work-in-progress)
- Add slide templates for partial renewals (mid-term upsell windows).
- Create a one-page health snapshot generator (script) pulling from billing + metrics APIs — assign to Solutions Eng backlog.
- Map standard concession thresholds to newly launched Dedicated pricing bands.

CHANGELOG
- 2025-11-12: Draft created (Aisha)
- 2026-01-07: Added Risk Scoring rubric and Renewal Tracker example (Marcus)
- 2026-02-28: Enterprise breakout templates expanded; moved to in_review (Evelyn)

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Might want to fold in a "customer ROI calculator" tab later — quick win for mid-market deals.
- Feel free to rip visuals from the product ops slide bank but avoid reusing verbatim language from existing QBR decks.

References: Confluence QBR framework (linked above), JIRA-1247 for tracker automation, sample contract language in /legal/sales/renewal-terms.

-----END OF KIT-----

(Really rough — treat as collaborative template. Placeholders like <Name> and <dates> should be replaced before sending.)
